unit: one row per identified contig taken to the gene level
question: how far was each identified contig from the reference that identified it, which the cascade computes and then discards
a_row_is: a distance and a coverage. There is no score on this table.

identity_distribution.readout: contigs per five-point identity bin, over every identified contig with a significant protein hit. This is the shape that says whether a line can be drawn or only a ranking
identity_distribution.null_reading: 304 of 11361 shuffled contigs clear the same significance bar, against 10170 real

gene_count_matched_spread.readout: median per-contig gene identity spread at equal numbers of scorable genes. The unmatched comparison is biased towards the divergent arm, whose contigs are longer and carry more genes

discrimination.readout: existence of a significant alignment, then every property of that alignment, real against a dinucleotide-preserving shuffle of the same contigs through the same search

existence.reading: 89.52% of real contigs against 2.68% of shuffles. The existence of the alignment is the calibrated quantity

conditional_on_a_hit.readout: share of real hits above the shuffled null's p90, per field. A null p90 puts 10% above it by construction, so 10% is the no-information level and the whole table has to be read against that number
conditional_on_a_hit.reading: cannot discriminate here. The strongest field is contig_coverage at 26.34% against a no-information level of 10%, and identity itself reads 11.98%. Once a shuffle clears the significance bar its alignment looks like a real one on every field measured, so no property of a hit may be used to argue that the hit is real

at_a_stricter_operating_point.readout: the same two piles under coverage and length floors. This is the only lever that moves the null, and it costs real hits, so the trade is reported rather than chosen here

operating_point.null: dinucleotide-preserving shuffle of the same contigs, same search

bands.reading: divergent strain of the named taxon
same genus or thereabouts, not a strain
family-level or looser; the subject is a nearest neighbour, not an identification
below any band a name survives

external_positive_control.what: the holdout thread's withheld genome: it assembles as one contig covering 96% of the withheld reference and hits it at 66.5% protein identity over 620 aa, and the cascade removes it as identified in tier 1
external_positive_control.scope: a different library, so this is an operating point and not a row in this table. The older mutated-spike ladder is a reference point rather than ground truth for a real distance.

blind_spots: whole-contig protein identity does not separate real sequence from a dinucleotide shuffle of it: the null's median identity is as low as the real one, because a chance alignment to a narrow index is short and lands wherever it lands. Read identity only beside alignment length and subject coverage, which is what the discrimination block reports

6.1% of dinucleotide shuffles clear E<1e-5 at 60 aa, which is high for a null. The untested candidate is low-complexity sequence, which a shuffle preserves and which aligns to anything; the control is the aligner's own compositional masking, not run here. Until that is measured the null rate is an upper bound on chance and the 16x existence ratio a lower bound
every identity here comes from RefSeq viral proteins plus Swiss-Prot, which are narrow, so each is an UPPER BOUND on distance from what is known
this says nothing about whether a divergent contig is a new species: demarcation criteria are per family and nothing here fetches them
protein identity understates nucleotide divergence because synonymous changes are invisible to it
a contig is already a consensus over reads and hides within-sample strain mixtures below about 3.8% divergence
the gene-level arm is capped by contig length, so a short divergent contig may carry a whole-contig distance and no gene-level row
